_meta.purpose: Per-state CPA license reinstatement cost + penalty-CPE data: what a lapsed CPA actually owes to get reinstated (fee + catch-up CPE hours + ethics hours), sourced fresh -- this dataset did not exist anywhere on the site before 2026-07-25. Same 2-source verification standard as cpa_deadlines.json and cpe_hours.json: a board page + a codified rule/statute for every record. A state whose real-world fee/hours figure is a formula (not a flat number) reports null in the numeric field and explains the formula in the matching *_notes field and data_gap_note -- never a guessed point figure.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Not a flat fee. Code of Ala. 1975 §34-1-11(d) lets the Board set a reinstatement fee (not exceeding $100) plus back registration fees and late penalties for every lapsed year -- the Board's own fee schedule sets the annual permit fee at $100 (individual)/$130 (firm) and late penalties of $100 (if filed January 1 through the last day of February) or $500 (if filed March 1-31), per 30-X-3-.07(4), compounding per lapsed year.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Formula: Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-5-.02(3)-(4) requires 40 CPE hours for EACH year off active status, capped at 120 hours (3+ lapsed years), with 20% in accounting & auditing, earned within the 3 years preceding the request.
records.lapse_trigger: Annual permits expire September 30; renewal (application, fee, CPE proof) is due by December 31. A $100 late penalty applies if filed Jan 1-Feb 28/29, a $500 late penalty if filed Mar 1-31. Failing to renew or apply for inactive status within 6 months of expiration (roughly by the following March 31) is itself grounds for revocation under Code of Ala. §34-1-11(d), after which formal reinstatement (a Board hearing) plus back-fees and catch-up CPE apply.
records.citation: Code of Alabama 1975, §34-1-11(d) (reinstatement fee & lapse/revocation trigger); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.07 (annual permit fees & late penalties); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-5-.02(3)-(4) (catch-up CPE hours)
records.data_gap_note: Heads-up: the underlying statute (Code of Ala. 1975 Sec 34-1-11) was amended by Act 2026-16 effective October 1, 2026 -- if you are reinstating on or after that date, check the revised text or confirm with the board, as these figures reflect the law in force before the amendment.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: $300 biennial renewal fee (12 AAC 02.340(4)) plus $100 delayed-renewal penalty (12 AAC 02.340(13)), once a license has lapsed more than 60 days -- covers the common under-1-year lapse. For a longer lapse (1-3 years), the $300 renewal fee is owed for EACH lapsed biennial period, so the total scales up; a lapse of 5+ years cannot be reinstated at all.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: For a lapse of 1+ years: 120 hours of approved CE completed in the 36 months preceding the reinstatement application (vs. the normal 80 hours/2 years) -- no more than 16 of those hours may be micro-learning. A lapse under 1 year requires no extra CE beyond normal compliance.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses are biennial, expiring December 31 of odd-numbered years regardless of issuance date. Missing that deadline lapses the license immediately; a $100 delayed-renewal penalty attaches once the lapse exceeds 60 days.
records.citation: 12 AAC 04.440(a)-(f) (Reinstatement of Lapsed License); fee amounts at 12 AAC 02.340(4),(13); license-term backdrop at 12 AAC 04.189

Read both rules directly (Cornell LII). 12 AAC 02.340(4) is the CPA biennial active license renewal fee, $300; (13) is the delayed renewal penalty fee, $100. 12 AAC 04.440(a) directs precisely those two for a license lapsed under one year and more than 60 days -- so $400 is the total the reinstatement rule actually produces, which is what this record's notes already show as arithmetic rather than as a single line item. The $400 figures the audit found in 02.340 are (8) and (9), both FIRM fees, unrelated. The $550 sum adds (12) license reactivation, $150, which applies to reactivating an INACTIVE license, not to reinstating a lapsed one -- 04.440 never calls for it. Fee and notes left unchanged. One real correction did come out of this: the citation listed subsection (12), which is not part of this determination, and has been dropped.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Same $100 application fee as new certification (Ariz. Admin. Code R4-1-341(A)(1)). Once reinstatement from canceled status is approved, the standard biennial registration fee ($100-$300, prorated) also applies -- total out-of-pocket can exceed $100.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Not a punitive add-on: up to 160 hours of CPE in the 4 years immediately before reinstating (R4-1-453(C)(7)) -- the same cumulative total a continuously-registered CPA owes over 4 years, capped even if the lapse ran longer.
records.lapse_trigger: Individual registration is biennial, keyed to the registrant's birth month with odd/even-year parity (R4-1-345). Missing the birth-month renewal deadline draws a $50 late fee; if still unrenewed, the certificate lapses to 'canceled' status, requiring reinstatement under A.R.S. §32-732(B). If 25-48 months have passed since the last renewal due date, the ethics-hour requirement doubles to 8 hours (vs. the normal 4).
records.citation: Ariz. Admin. Code R4-1-341(A)(1) (reinstatement fee); R4-1-453(C)(4),(7) (normal vs. reinstatement CPE/ethics hours); A.R.S. §32-732(B) (reinstatement from canceled status); R4-1-345(B)-(C) (birth-year-parity cycle)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Flat, non-refundable $150 reinstatement fee (Board Rule 12.2) if reinstated within 3 years of expiration -- distinct from the separate $25/month late-renewal fee that accrues in the first 3 months after the December 31 expiration, before the license actually lapses.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond the standard renewal formula for a sub-3-year lapse: 40 hours of CPE for each consecutive 12-month period lapsed (pro-rated at 3 1/3 hours/month), the same rate as ordinary renewal -- not an add-on penalty.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire annually on December 31. A monthly late fee accrues starting January 1; if still not renewed by April 1 of the following year, the license automatically LAPSES by operation of statute.
records.citation: Ark. Code Ann. § 17-12-504(f)-(h) (late fee, lapse trigger, 3-year reinstatement window); 17 CAR § 236-1101 (required fees; formerly Board Rule 12.2); 17 CAR § 236-1203 et seq. (CPE required for reinstatement; formerly Rule 13.7(d)/13.9)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: California calls this the 'delinquency fee,' not a separate line item -- $200 for a license expiring after June 30, 2026 ($170 before), equal to 50% of the $400/$340 renewal fee (Bus. & Prof. Code §163.5).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Formula: an additional 20 hours of CE for each full 6-month period between expiration and the renewal application date, capped at 80 additional hours on top of the normal 80-hour/2-year requirement. No extra CE if less than 6 full months have elapsed.
records.lapse_trigger: An individual permit expires at the end of the second year of a 2-year cycle anchored to the licensee's own birth month (Bus. & Prof. Code §5070.5). A delinquent (expired) permit may still be renewed for up to 5 years after expiration by paying all accrued fees plus the delinquency fee and showing CE compliance; after 5 years it can no longer be renewed at all.
records.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §5070.6 (delinquent renewal / 5-year window) and §5070.5 (permit expiration on birth-month); delinquency-fee formula at §163.5; extra CE at 16 CCR §81

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No dollar figure is codified anywhere -- C.R.S. 12-20-202 delegates fee-setting to the DORA Director, published only on the online licensing portal, not in statute or rule. There is simply no primary-law dollar figure to cite for this one.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 3 CCR 705-1 Rule 1.9(K)(1): the applicant must complete BOTH the full 80-hour requirement for the CPE period immediately preceding reinstatement, AND 10 hours for each full quarter the certificate was expired in the current period (up to 80 more) -- up to 160 hours total catch-up. These hours can't also count toward CPE owed for the remainder of the period after reinstatement.
records.lapse_trigger: A certificate not renewed by its expiration date enters 'Expired' status (Rule 1.9(J)(1)). A 60-day grace period allows renewal by paying the renewal fee plus a late fee with no penalty; after that, the certificate is fully Expired and the holder cannot hold out as a CPA.
records.citation: 3 CCR 705-1, Rule 1.9(J) (Expired Status) and Rule 1.9(K) (Reinstatement)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Regs. Conn. State Agencies §20-280-25(g) requires paying 'the current year's renewal fee' to reinstate a license lapsed more than 90 days (and up to 3 years) -- that fee is set by statute at $565: CGS Sec 20-281d(g) pegs it to the Class I professional services fee, and CGS Sec 33-182l sets Class I at $565.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 hours of CPE earned in the single year immediately preceding the reinstatement application (rather than spread over the normal cycle).
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire annually on December 31; a late application is accepted through January 31. If not received by February 1, the license lapses. Lapsed 90 days or less: reinstate by simple application. Lapsed more than 90 days but less than 3 years: reinstate at the department's discretion on the fee + 40-hour CPE terms above. Lapsed 3+ years: must apply for an entirely new license.
records.citation: Regs. Conn. State Agencies §20-280-25 (Renewal and reinstatement of license and continuing professional education requirement)
records.verification_history:

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Board's own fee page lists Renewal $110, Late Renewal $50, and Reinstatement $295 as distinct line items.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 17 DCMR §2530.3: reinstating a license lapsed less than 5 years requires 40 hours of approved CPE for each year of non-renewal, capped at 120 hours -- this replaces, not stacks on top of, the normal 80-hour/2-year requirement.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses are on a 2-year cycle expiring December 31 of even-numbered years. Failing to renew by that date lapses the license; DC's general licensing law separately tiers late penalties ($75/$150/$350) by how long a license has been lapsed, though the Board's own posted flat $295 reinstatement fee is the figure actually applied.
records.citation: 17 DCMR §2530.3 (reinstatement CPE); D.C. Code §47-2851.10 (lapsed and reinstated licenses); §47-2853.10 (Board fee-schedule authority)
records.data_gap_note: The $295 reinstatement fee is stated on the Board's own page, but no codified DCMR fee schedule or DC Register notice stating that exact number could be located -- only the general statutory authority for the Board to set fees. records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No fixed dollar figure is published. 24 Del. C. §124 requires the regular renewal fee plus an additional late/reinstatement processing fee (the Board's own fee page says the late fee equals 50% of the renewal fee) -- but the renewal fee itself isn't published as a fixed number ('you are notified of the amount at the time of renewal'), so no flat total can be honestly stated.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond the standard requirement: 24 Del. C. §124 requires only proof the standing 80-hour biennial requirement (24 Del. Admin. Code §100-7.2.1) has been met, not an additional amount.
records.lapse_trigger: Permits expire June 30 of odd-numbered years. A lapsed permit may be reinstated within 1 year of the lapse, at the Board's discretion; if not reinstated within that window, the permit terminates and the holder must reapply as a brand-new applicant.
records.citation: 24 Del. C. §124 (Renewals); §108 (expiration/renewal cycle); 24 Del. Admin. Code §100-7.2 (CPE requirements)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Reinstatement-of-a-null-and-void-license application fee (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-31.015). Reinstatement from null-and-void is discretionary (board must find good-faith effort defeated by illness/hardship, s. 473.313(1)(d), Fla. Stat., renumbered from the former subsection (5) by ch. 2024-97) -- not a routine online renewal. A separate $25 delinquent-status fee may also apply but could not be independently confirmed against a codified rule.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Two-step climb of 120 hours each (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-33.006): 120 hrs to move null-and-void back to delinquent, then another 120 hrs to move delinquent back to active. 160 hours above Florida's normal 80-hour biennial requirement; all must fall within the 24 months preceding the application.
records.lapse_trigger: License goes DELINQUENT on January 1 following failure to report CPE for biennial renewal; if not cured, remains delinquent for 2 years and then AUTOMATICALLY becomes NULL AND VOID (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-30.030), no further board action required.
records.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-31.015 ($250 reinstatement fee); r. 61H1-30.030 (2-year automatic null-and-void trigger); r. 61H1-30.030(4)(a)-(b) (120+120-hr CPE, 8 ethics hrs/step); s. 473.313(1)(d), Fla. Stat. (discretionary reinstatement, renumbered from (5) by ch. 2024-97)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: $300 reinstatement fee (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 20-10-.04(1)(a)), payable in addition to completing the CPE catch-up requirement. For that catch-up, the rule also requires at least 20% of the hours in accounting/auditing, at least 80 of the hours within the 2 years preceding the application, and bars carryover hours from counting toward reinstatement.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 hours of CPE for each year since the license last renewed, capped at 160 hours (double the normal 80-hour/2-year renewal). At least 20% of the total must be in accounting/auditing subjects, and at least 80 hours must fall within the 2 years immediately preceding the application; no carryover allowed.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire December 31 of odd-numbered years. A 4-month penalty period follows, during which the license can still be renewed by paying a $100 penalty fee plus the renewal fee. After that window closes, reinstatement (not renewal) is required.
records.citation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 20-10-.04 (Reinstatement); r. 20-10-.02 (Biennial Renewal); r. 20-10-.03 (Penalty Period/Late Renewal)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: IDAPA 24.30.01.400 sets the reinstatement fee as the sum of unpaid license fees for the preceding 3 cycles -- $360 is the representative case (3 x $120 active annual fee), varying with how many cycles were missed. Idaho Code §54-212(6) caps the total at $500.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: IDAPA 24.30.01.117: 80 hours of CPE completed within the 12 months immediately before applying for reinstatement -- the same 80-hour total as normal renewal, just compressed from a 2-year cycle into a single 12-month lookback window.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire June 30 each year. Renewing after July 1 but before August 1 only requires a $100 late fee; if still unrenewed by August 1, the license is deemed lapsed and subject to reinstatement, and the holder may not use the CPA title or perform reserved services.
records.citation: IDAPA 24.30.01.117 (Reinstatement and Re-entry); 24.30.01.108 (Annual Renewal and Late Fee); 24.30.01.400 (Fees) -- current post-2023-renumbering
